answer: Collapse look-alike answers before paying. Each epoch, every submission is fingerprinted and grouped by near-duplicate similarity; a whole group splits one reward, yet each account inside it still posts its own copper-sized entry stake. Fifty puppets rewording one template earn what a single honest account earns while paying fifty stakes, so a farm's payoff reaches its zenith at one account and falls with every extra head. The clustering works like a lantern on the backlog: copies become visible, and unprofitable.
